transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-21
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah, Marco Diaz, Claire Bennett (Redwood) — Dana Lee, Miguel Torres, Ayesha Khan, Tom Riddell (Solaris)

[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll get started in a minute. Hi Dana, hi Miguel, hi team, great to meet you all. This is our onboarding kickoff, I'll run the agenda quickly, Marco will cover the VPC/tech details, Claire will cover security and support, and we'll wrap with next steps.
[00:35] Dana Lee: Hi, thanks Priya, excited to get this going. Quick note — we're looking to move a couple of generative features to production by Q4 so want to make sure infra and security line up.
[01:20] Priya Shah: Awesome, high-level timeline is we do a two-week Dedicated trial to validate latency/cost, then a 4-6 week implementation for production roll, that fits your Q4 timeline?
[01:45] Miguel Torres: Yep that seems fine; our main constraints: VPC peering rules, audit logs retention, and we need SSO integration. Also curious about quantization/throughput recommendations — we use a mix of T4s and a small A100 pool.
[02:30] Marco Diaz: Got it. For the trial we can provision Dedicated pool that matches your numbers; we typically recommend a mix of batching and KV prefix cache. Note: our runtime supports quantized model variants, but perf varies by model and sequence length.
[03:10] Tom Riddell: Can you clarify hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Our security lead wants VPC and KMS at minimum.
[03:45] Claire Bennett: Real quick — Hosted is fastest to get started (managed infra, less control), Dedicated is reserved capacity with tenant isolation and predictable latency, and Private is on-prem/VPC with customer-managed networking and KMS integration. For Solaris, sounds like Dedicated or Private are options; Dedicated supports customer VPC peering and KMS for key wrapping.
[04:30] Ayesha Khan: When you say KMS integration, do you support our AWS KMS/HSM? We need envelope encryption and key rotation logs. Also, do you provide audit logs that meet our retention policy of 2 years?
[05:10] Claire Bennett: Yes we integrate with customer KMS for keys; audit logs are covered but retention beyond 90 days is an add-on — we can include extended retention as part of the enterprise package. I'll share the SOC2 pack and retention options after the call.
[06:00] Priya Shah: We'll put that in the next steps. Miguel, can you give a quick overview of expected qps, latency SLOs, and typical request sizes?
[06:20] Miguel Torres: Sure — average qps for our chat assistant ~8 qps with peaks to 50 during daytime. Median request length ~120 tokens, long tails to 1k tokens for agent transcripts. Latency SLOs target 300-500ms for first token ideally, but we'll trade cost if needed.
[07:05] Marco Diaz: Good detail; based on that we'd start with a few A100-backed instances for headroom during peak. For 50 qps with 1k tails we'll look at autoscaling policies; Redwood's runtime can do continuous batching but there's a latency tradeoff. We'll craft a policy to keep p50 latency inside your 300-500ms target while controlling token cost.
[07:50] Dana Lee: Can you run benchmarks against our model? We plan to use an open model variant, possibly quantized.
[08:20] Marco Diaz: Absolutely, we can run benchmark tests during the trial — we'll need a sample model and representative prompts. If you can share a small eval suite we'll run perf and cost numbers and return a spreadsheet with token-level cost breakdowns.
[08:55] Tom Riddell: Are there any gotchas with our infra? We have strict egress rules and only a few whitelisted endpoints for peering.
[09:30] Marco Diaz: For VPC peering we need a short list of endpoints/IPs and cross-account role for provisioning. We can do private link in some regions if peering is impossible. We'll send a network checklist.
[10:05] Ayesha Khan: Also, do you support SAML SSO for console access and RBAC for teams? We need SCIM provisioning ideally.
[10:30] Claire Bennett: Yes SSO via SAML is supported; we also have RBAC and SCIM. I'll include the SSO config doc.
[11:00] Priya Shah: On pricing — trial will be free for the two-week Dedicated provision but we will share estimated cost models. Post-trial pricing will be usage-based plus reserved capacity pricing if you go Dedicated.
[11:35] Miguel Torres: How do you handle model rollouts and fallback? We sometimes need canary testing and quick fallback to smaller models if latency spikes.
[12:05] Marco Diaz: Redwood supports rollouts and automatic fallback policies — you can pin production routes to a primary model and have a cheaper, lower-latency fallback. We also have built-in tracing and token-level cost dashboards so you can see regression quickly.
[12:45] Dana Lee: For data privacy, do you retain user data? We need no retention of PII in logs, and guarantee that customer data isn't used to train public models.
[13:15] Claire Bennett: By default we retain logs for 90 days; we can set zero-retention for request/response logs during the trial if that helps. And we do not use customer data to train public models — we can sign that into the contract.
[13:55] Tom Riddell: Great. Any required legal or procurement items we should prep?
[14:20] Priya Shah: We'll send an initial MSA and a security addendum; procurement typically wants SOC2 report, DPIA if needed, and the network checklist.
[14:50] Miguel Torres: For the benchmark, our ML team needs an approximate timeline — how long to get trial provisioned and benchmarks run?
[15:10] Marco Diaz: We can provision Dedicated in 2-3 business days once we have network info and the cross-account role. Benchmarks typically take 2-4 business days depending on eval size. So end-to-end about one week to get actionable numbers.
[15:45] Dana Lee: OK sounds good. On the model side we'll share a small eval set and a quantized model artifact link. One question — does Redwood do on-the-fly quantization or do you expect us to supply quantized weights?
[16:20] Marco Diaz: We can run both. For the trial we usually test the customer's preferred variant. If you want we can run both fp16 and quantized paths to show perf/cost tradeoffs. Some models see smaller accuracy delta, but it's model-dependent.
[17:00] Ayesha Khan: Does the Dedicated environment allow us to rotate keys and have audit logs routed to our SIEM?
[17:25] Claire Bennett: Yes — you can route audit logs to your S3 or SIEM, and we support customer-managed KMS with key rotation. I'll include integration docs.
[17:55] Tom Riddell: Any limitations on sequence length with prefix caching and KV cache? We're concerned about cost for long transcripts.
[18:30] Marco Diaz: We support KV cache and prefix caching; for very long transcripts we recommend chunking or summarization pre-processing. The runtime handles KV eviction policies; we'll show suggested configs.
[19:05] Priya Shah: Ok let's recap next steps: Claire will send SOC2 and SSO docs, Marco will share the network checklist and benchmarking plan, I'll send onboarding playbook and pricing. We'll also provision a 2-week Dedicated trial once Solaris provides network info.
[19:35] Miguel Torres: I'll share traffic profile and whitelisted endpoints by Friday.
[20:00] Dana Lee: We'll also invite our infra team to the VPC deep-dive next week.
[20:20] Priya Shah: Great — thanks everyone. Any final questions?
[20:30] Ayesha Khan: One tiny ask — can you include an example of what token-level cost reporting looks like?
[20:45] Marco Diaz: Yes we'll attach a recent benchmark spreadsheet with token-level breakdowns.
[21:10] Priya Shah: Perfect. We'll send notes and action items right after. Thanks all.
[21:25] End of recording (note: automated transcript may mislabel some acronyms).

Notes about transcription: occasional misspellings and mis-attributed speaker tags possible (e.g., 'KV cache' occasionally transcribed as 'kay vee cache', 'KMS' sometimes 'kms').
